outcome: Give plant manager / operations excellence director a governed method to improve unmanaged OT device share using passive network observations, PLC firmware and site registers, with final decisions…
overview: Industrial OT Asset Inventory and Drift addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in manufacturing operations. The first proof of value uses passive network observations, PLC firmware and site registers. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is unmanaged OT device share, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: passive network observations, PLC firmware and site registers; define unmanaged OT device share and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Plant Manager / Operations Excellence Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
